To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We have produced six rat mAbs against EGFR and are investigating their potential as therapeutic reagents for the treatment of human tumours overexpressing the receptors.

(i) the six new rat mAb bind to the extracellular region of the EGFR, (ii) the mAbs inhibit the growth of tumours that over express the EGFR but have no effect on tumour lines that express little or no EGFR, and (iii) the mAbs are effective in vivo in inhibiting the growth of tumour xenografts in athymic nude mice.
we have produced six rat monoclonal anti-EGFR antibodies that bind to the external domain of this receptor and inhibit growth of tumour cells in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production and characterisation of new monoclonal antibodies against the human EFG receptor (EGFR).
the development of a new generation of antibodies against the human EGR receptor for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes.
the development and application of new mAbs against the human EGFR and their use in the diagnosis and treatment of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mAbs described here are potentially valuable for the diagnosis and treatment of tumours overexpressing EGFR.
the mAbs are useful tools to study the role of the EGFR in the growth and differentiation of human tumours and may be useful for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes.
the mAbs described in this study have potential for use in the treatment of patients with squamous carcinoma of the head and neck and breast carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antibodies are useful tools to study the EGFR and that they may have therapeutic value in patients whose tumours express high levels of the receptor.
we have produced a number of new rat monoclonnal antibodies against the EGFR and have investigated their use for diagnostic applications in cancer patients.
we have produced six rat mAbs that bind to the extracellular portion of the EGFR on human tumour cell lines and inhibit the growth stimulation of quiescent fibroblasts by EGF and TFG alpha.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have developed a new generation of antibodies that bind with high affinity, block growth factor receptor interaction, and inhibit the growth and proliferation of human squamous cell carcinoma cell lines that overexpress the EGFR.
the human EGFR is a target for cancer treatment and that the mAb approach is a viable strategy for the development of new therapeutic agents.
the EGFR can be targeted with antibodies and this has potential for cancer therapy.
